analysis:
All supplied changes are documentation. The new report docs/reports/2026-10-21-mixed-step-prefill-geometry.md and the index update in docs/reports/README.md add measurement evidence only. The configuration.md change (patch excerpt at head lines 393-395) swaps the DARKBLOOM_CBV2_SOLO_PREFILL_STRIPE row for DARKBLOOM_CBV2_PREFILL_CHUNK; its full text is truncated, and the head units supplied (lines 483-705) contain no changed lines. No code, trust boundary, authentication, attestation, encryption, coordinator protocol or cache storage behavior is altered in the evidence I received.

Security-relevant observations, none of which qualify as a finding:
- The report describes a larger default prefill geometry for Gemma 4 (2048-token chunk, 4096-token step budget). It documents that activation peaks can exceed the reserve floor for GPT-OSS and dense Qwen at 32k prompts, and that p99 and max inter-token gaps grow. That is why the wide geometry is not their default. This relates to availability and memory admission (T-016 and T-029 are loosely adjacent). The Gemma default stays 1.77 GiB inside its floor, and the document states the memory-pressure risk and the opt-in scope.
- The report mentions a media ceiling of 512 for Gemma 4 vision requests in the production default. The implementing code is not supplied, so I could not verify that the ceiling exists. This is an unverified contract, not evidence of a regression.
- The documented opt-in environment variables are not forwarded by the LaunchAgent (stated elsewhere in configuration.md), so they do not expand the daemon attack surface.
- The prefix-cache rows in configuration.md (T-041 context) are unchanged context, and the new report states that its load arms used no prefix reuse, so it makes no new cache-timing claims.

Remaining question for later passes: the code that sets the Gemma wide-geometry default and media ceiling (EngineV2Factory+Configuration.swift) is outside this batch. If it ships in the same PR, it should be checked against the admission and memory-floor assumptions.
